title: Window and Door Rebates in Prince George 2026: $100 Each, Up to $2,000
desc: BC Hydro pays $100 per window or door in Prince George, up to $2,000. 62% of households live in pre-1981 homes and January lows average -9.7°C.
h1: Window and Door Rebates in Prince George
lead: Prince George has old homes and long winters. Replacing old windows here pays a rebate of $100 per opening and makes a real difference on a -30°C night.
cards_heading: What BC Hydro pays for windows and doors in Prince George
cards_intro: We re-read BC Hydro's window and door page on October 2, 2026. The rebate is for homes heated mainly by electricity. FortisBC lists $100 per opening for its gas customers, except in the City of Vancouver.

cards.title: Windows and doors
cards.note: Paid for each window or door that replaces an existing one between a heated space and outdoors.

cards.title: Cap
cards.note: That is 20 openings at $100 each. A bay window counts as one opening.

cards.title: Energy rating
cards.note: The window or door must have a maximum U-factor of 1.22 W/m2-K, which is BC Hydro's Tier 2 level.

cards.title: More than one upgrade
cards.note: BC Hydro adds a bonus when you finish more than one eligible upgrade.

cards.title: Lower incomes
cards.note: Income-qualified customers can apply for free upgrades.

after_cards:
A Prince George 1960s house

A two-storey with 14 windows, a front door and a back door is 16 openings. That pays $1,600. Pair it with insulation in the same application and you can ask BC Hydro about the multi-upgrade bonus.
sections: The 2021 Census counted 31,795 households in Prince George. About 19,610 (62%) live in homes built before 1981, and 10,470 are owner-occupied detached houses from that period. Detached houses are 58% of households and 17% live in apartments. About 6.5% say their home needs major repairs.

Prince George's average January low from 2015 to 2024 was -9.7°C, and the coldest day was -42.4°C. Windows from before 1981 are more likely to have early double glazing or none at all. Check the label on yours, because a window that was fine for a 1970s code may be well below the 1.22 W/m2-K rebate level.

The home must be mainly electric-heated, at least 12 months old and a primary residence. The BC Hydro account holder applies, or signs a consent form for someone else to apply. Condos and apartments use a separate program.
Each rough opening counts as one. A bay window is one. Skylights are excluded. Units need a U-factor of 1.22 W/m2-K or lower and a listing from CSA, Intertek, Labtest, QAI or NFRC.

The rebate needs a U-factor of 1.22 W/m2-K or lower, and lower means less heat loss. Many window labels show the older imperial scale instead. To convert, multiply the imperial number by 5.678. A label that says U-0.30 equals 1.70 W/m2-K, which is too high. A label that says U-0.21 equals about 1.19 W/m2-K and passes. Ask the contractor to quote the metric value for each model so you do not have to convert.

BC Hydro publishes a consumer guide for window and door replacement. It covers frame materials, glazing types and what to ask a contractor. Read it before you take quotes, so you can compare units on the same terms. The program only checks the U-factor, certification and installation rules, so the other choices are yours.

BC Hydro sends income-qualified customers to the CleanBC Better Homes Energy Savings Program instead, and the two cannot be combined. The 2026 program document lists no insulation or window rebates, so the free Energy Conservation Assistance Program is the route to ask about.
claim_heading: How to claim in Prince George
claim_steps: Check the home is electric-heated and at least 12 months old.
Get quotes that list the U-factor of each unit.
Photograph each label on installation day.
Keep the invoice and apply within six months.
Add insulation to the same application to check the bonus.
